altered CS ending in rising scale; soprano repeats bass of ep.1 rising by ninths; jerky rhythm in middle

countersubjects.notes: does not occur again in original form until bar 50; drastically changed in its six other appearances (13, 24, 30, 42, 60, 72); broken-chord figures spread over two voices (p.16)

subject.notes: dominant strongly accented at beginning of bar 2 but approached by upward steps, so a tonal answer is impossible

claims.claim: Exposition entries delayed by codettas at bars 6 and 12.
Codetta joins subject to CS; approached by octave (6, 29, 77), seventh (12, 18, 35, 47, 65) or minor ninth (55).
CS appears in original form only at bar 50 after the exposition; drastically changed in six other appearances.
Episode 5 stops abruptly on a pause on the dominant (bar 70).
